plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely grown in gardens and fields and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Its flowers are harvested for essential oils, sachets, and culinary use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region, cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round, water-repellent leaves held above the water and spectacular fragrant flowers on tall stalks. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes, and slow-moving waters and is revered in many cultures.
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan, and northern Australia; widely cultivated in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that causes water and dirt to roll off, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect' that inspires self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy North American prairie perennial with daisy-like flowers featuring drooping petals around a prominent spiky orange-brown central cone. It thrives in full sun, tolerates drought, and attracts pollinators, then provides seeds for goldfinches in autumn.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; cultivated in gardens across temperate regions
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone of the flower.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic evergreen shrub producing the largest flower heads in the Proteaceae family, with a central cluster of tiny flowers surrounded by colorful, petal-like bracts. It grows in the fynbos vegetation and is adapted to fire and nutrient-poor soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom in late winter and spring, with flowering from about May to November in the Southern Hemisphere, including late June
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and its lineage is ancient, with the Proteaceae family dating back more than 300 million years to the supercontinent Gondwana.
